questions.question: Which generative model family produces samples without ever writing down a closed-form expression for the data density p(x)?
questions.explanation: GANs are implicit-density models: they learn a generator G(z) that produces samples, but there is no way to evaluate p(x) for a given point. The other three families all provide (or bound) an explicit log p(x).

questions.question: A VAE optimizes which objective as a proxy for log p(x)?
options: Binary cross-entropy between real and fake
The score function of the data distribution
questions.explanation: VAEs optimize the ELBO, a tractable lower bound on log p(x) composed of a reconstruction term minus a KL divergence. This puts VAEs in the 'explicit density, approximate' family.

questions.question: According to the lesson taxonomy, diffusion models belong to which density family?
questions.explanation: Diffusion models (DDPM) optimize a weighted ELBO — a lower bound on log p(x) — placing them in the 'explicit density, approximate' category alongside VAEs.

questions.question: Which family is described as the dominant backbone for image, video, and 3D generation in 2026?
questions.explanation: Score-based and flow-matching models (Stable Diffusion 3, Flux, AudioCraft 2) are described as the 2024-2026 standard for image, video, and 3D, offering faster sampling than DDPM via straighter ODE paths.

questions.question: What is the primary inference-cost advantage of GAN-based models over diffusion-based models in production?
options: GANs use a single forward pass with no iterative sampling
questions.explanation: GANs generate a sample with one forward pass through G(z), so TTFT equals total latency. Diffusion models require num_steps x step_cost, making GANs far cheaper for narrow-domain, latency-sensitive tasks.

questions.question: Which year did the DDPM paper by Ho, Jain, and Abbeel make diffusion models practical for image generation?
questions.explanation: Ho, Jain, Abbeel published DDPM in 2020, simplifying the training loss to plain MSE on noise prediction and demonstrating state-of-the-art sample quality.
